characters.name: Frodo Baggins
clues: Both of this character's parents died in a boating accident long before any adventure began.
A beloved older relative adopted this character, then left behind his home and a small golden trinket.
A wound from a cursed blade, taken beneath a ruined watchtower on a hill, never fully healed.
At a council in Rivendell, this character volunteered to carry a dangerous object to the land where it was made.
At the Cracks of Doom this character could not give up the Ring willingly, and lost a finger to the creature who seized it.

references.supports: Parents died in a boating accident; adopted by Bilbo; Morgul-knife wound on Weathertop; volunteered at the Council of Elrond; finger bitten off by Gollum at Mount Doom.

characters.name: Samwise Gamgee
clues: Raised by a gardener, this character loved plants, tales of the Elves and a quiet life.
Caught eavesdropping beneath a window, this character was sent on a journey instead of being punished.
A small box of soil from an elven queen's forest later brought trees back to a ravaged homeland.
When a giant spider seemed to have killed his master, this character took up the burden himself for a time.
This character carried his master up the slopes of Mount Doom when strength failed, and later served many terms as Mayor of the Shire.

references.supports: Gardener's son; overheard by Gandalf under the window; Galadriel's gift of earth; took the Ring in Cirith Ungol; carried Frodo up Mount Doom; Mayor of the Shire.

characters.name: Gandalf
clues: One of a handful of beings who came from across the Sea in the guise of an old man, sent to guide rather than to rule.
A wanderer with a fondness for fireworks, rarely seen without his pipe.
This character fell in battle with a fire-demon on a bridge in the deep dark, and returned in a brighter form.
This character bore a ring of fire, given long before by the shipwright of the Grey Havens.
Clad in grey, then in white after returning from death, this wizard rode Shadowfax, lord of horses.

references.supports: One of the Istari; fireworks; usually seen with a pipe; fall on the Bridge of Khazad-dûm and return as Gandalf the White; Narya passed to him by Círdan; rode Shadowfax.

characters.name: Aragorn
clues: Raised in secret by an elf-lord, this character was long hidden under a different name.
Heir to a line of kings that traced its descent from Elendil, though no king had ruled that line's realm for ages.
A Ranger of the North, this character guided four small travelers through the wild lands of Eriador.
This character looked into a seeing-stone and openly challenged the Dark Lord.
Crowned king of both Gondor and Arnor, this character wed Arwen, daughter of Elrond.

references.supports: Fostered in Rivendell under another name; descent from Elendil; Ranger who guided the hobbits from Bree; used the Orthanc-stone to show himself to Sauron; crowned King of the Reunited Kingdom; married Arwen.

characters.name: Legolas
clues: The son of a king, this character was sent from a northern forest realm to carry news to Rivendell.
Light of foot, this character could walk on top of snow without sinking, on a mountain pass in winter.
This character and a Dwarf became fast friends, though their peoples had long been at odds.
At the cries of seabirds, this character first felt the call of the Sea that no Elf can long resist.
The only Elf among the nine travelers, this archer shot down the winged steed of a Ringwraith over the Great River.

references.supports: Son of Thranduil; messenger to Rivendell; walked on snow on Caradhras; friendship with Gimli; heard gulls at Pelargir; shot the Nazgûl's steed over the Anduin.

characters.name: Gimli
clues: This character's father had been one of the company that once set out to reclaim a mountain from a dragon.
This character asked an elven lady for a single strand of her hair and was given three.
Alongside a Ranger and an Elf, this character ran for days across wide plains in pursuit of a band of Orcs.
At a great fortress in a mountain valley, this character fought on the wall, and afterwards marveled at the glittering caves behind it.
Many years after the War of the Ring, this character sailed West in the company of an Elf who had become his closest friend.

references.supports: Son of Glóin of Thorin's company; three strands of Galadriel's hair; pursuit across Rohan; Helm's Deep and the Glittering Caves; fought beside Legolas; sailed West (Fo.A. 120).

characters.name: Gollum
clues: This character's life was ruined by the murder of a friend over a gleaming find in a riverbed.
Exiled from his own kin, this character lived for centuries in the dark beneath a mountain range, eating raw fish.
A riddle contest with a stranger in the dark ended with the loss of the only thing this character cared for.
This character guided two travelers toward a mountain of fire, torn between a sworn oath and a terrible craving.
At the Cracks of Doom this character bit off a finger to take the Ring, then toppled into the fire with it.

references.supports: Murdered Déagol over the Ring; exiled and lived under the Misty Mountains; riddle game with Bilbo; guided Frodo and Sam to Mordor; bit off Frodo's finger and fell into the fire.

characters.name: Sauron
clues: Before turning to evil, this being served a smith among the Powers and loved order and craft.
Posing as a fair emissary, this being taught the Elven-smiths of a western land to make rings.
This being allowed himself to be carried captive to a great island, then corrupted its king until the island was swallowed by the sea.
At the end of the Second Age, a prince cut a ring from this being's hand with the broken blade of his father's sword.
Ruler of Mordor from the Dark Tower, served by nine Ringwraiths and symbolized by a lidless eye.

references.supports: Maia of Aulë; fair guise and the Rings of Power; captivity in Númenor and its Downfall; Isildur cut the Ring from his hand; Barad-dûr, Nazgûl, the Eye.

characters.name: Galadriel
clues: Born in the Blessed Realm, this character had seen a light that no longer shines.
This character ruled a realm of golden-leaved trees alongside her husband.
This character kept a basin of water that showed things that were, things that are, and things that yet may be.
A small traveler offered this character the Ring of Power, and she pictured herself as a terrible queen before refusing it.
Bearer of Nenya, the ring of adamant, this character gave the Fellowship cloaks, gifts, and a phial holding the light of a star.

references.supports: Born in Aman and saw the Two Trees; ruled Lothlórien with Celeborn; Mirror of Galadriel; refused the Ring; bearer of Nenya; gifts to the Fellowship including the Phial.
Lothlórien described as a golden wood with mallorn trees.

characters.name: Boromir
clues: The elder of two sons of a Steward, this character was admired by many and the pride of his father.
This character carried a great horn, tipped with silver, and sounded it in a time of need.
A recurring dream that troubled his family sent this character north through hard country to a council in Rivendell.
At a council this character argued that the Ring should be used as a weapon in the defense of his city.
This character died at Amon Hen defending two hobbits from Orcs, after he had tried to take the Ring by force.

references.supports: Elder son of Denethor; great horn tipped with silver, sounded in Moria; dream and journey to Rivendell; argued at the Council of Elrond; died defending Merry and Pippin at Amon Hen after trying to seize the Ring.

characters.name: Bilbo Baggins
clues: This character was a respectable, comfort-loving soul until an unexpected party of guests changed everything.
This character was hired as a burglar by a company seeking to reclaim a mountain and its treasure.
In a dark cave, this character won a game of riddles and walked away with a magic ring.
This character wrote the story of his journey, which later became part of the Red Book of Westmarch.
After vanishing from his own eleventy-first birthday party, this character eventually left Middle-earth over the Sea.

references.supports: Hired as burglar by Thorin's company; riddle game; found the Ring; authored the Red Book material; vanished at his 111th birthday; sailed West.

characters.name: Saruman
clues: Head of an order sent from across the Sea, this character was a deep student of the lore of the Rings.
This character made his home in a black tower inside a ringed fortress, where he kept a seeing-stone.
Gazing into a stone of far-seeing, this character was ensnared by his greater enemy and betrayed his task.
This character's fires felled forests, and in pits beneath his tower he bred a stronger kind of Orc.
After his fall, this character took over the Shire in disguise, and was finally killed by his own former servant.

references.supports: Head of the Istari; Orthanc and its palantír; corruption through the palantír; felling of trees and Uruk-hai; occupation of the Shire and death at Gríma's hand.

characters.name: Faramir
clues: The younger of two brothers, this character was a lover of lore and music who was overlooked by his father.
This character captained a company of Rangers who ambushed enemy soldiers in a green land west of Mordor.
In a hidden refuge behind a waterfall, this character questioned two hobbits and, though tempted by their burden, let them go.
After a doomed sortie ordered by his father, this character lay near death, struck down by the Black Breath.
Healed in the Houses of Healing, this character fell in love with a shieldmaiden of Rohan, and was later raised to a princely title in the land he had defended.

references.supports: Younger son of Denethor, lover of lore; Captain of the Rangers of Ithilien; Henneth Annûn and Frodo; Black Breath after Osgiliath; married Éowyn and became Prince of Ithilien.

characters.name: Éowyn
clues: This character's greatest fear was not death but being left behind in a life of dull duty.
This character's brother was imprisoned for disobedience on the orders of a sly advisor.
In disguise, this character rode into war with a small hobbit on her saddle.
This character confronted the Lord of the Nazgûl and declared herself no man, fulfilling an old prophecy.
This character put down the sword, learned the arts of healing, and married a prince of Ithilien.

references.supports: Fear of a cage; rode as Dernhelm with Merry; slew the Witch-king; healed and married Faramir.
On Gríma's orders Éomer was arrested and imprisoned for his disobedience.

characters.name: Théoden
clues: This ruler aged before his time under the whispered influence of a servant who served another master.
A wizard freed this ruler from a weakened state, and he stood tall again.
This ruler's only son and heir fell in battle against a wizard's forces at a river crossing.
This ruler retreated to a fortress in a mountain valley, where his people won a battle that earned him a new name meaning the Renewed.
This ruler died on the Pelennor Fields, crushed by his fallen horse, after leading a great charge at dawn.

references.supports: Under Gríma's influence; healed by Gandalf; Théodred fell at the Fords of Isen; retreated to Helm's Deep, won the Battle of the Hornburg and became known as Ednew, the Renewed; death on the Pelennor Fields beneath Snowmane.

characters.name: Elrond
clues: This character's twin brother chose a mortal life, and he chose to remain among the Elves.
As a child, this character was taken captive in the sack of his parents' haven, yet came to love one of his captors, a son of an ancient smith.
This character served as herald to the High King in a great war at the end of the Second Age.
This character healed a hobbit of a wound from a cursed blade and presided over a council deciding the fate of the Ring.
Master of a hidden valley, bearer of the ring of sapphire, this character was the father of Arwen.

references.supports: Twin Elros chose mortality; taken captive at the sack of the Havens and came to love Maglor; herald of Gil-galad; healed Frodo; Council of Elrond; bearer of Vilya; father of Arwen.

characters.name: Treebeard
clues: This character and his kin learned to speak from the Elves, in a time when the world was young.
A shepherd of trees who never says anything in haste, this character had long lost his wife.
This character took two hobbits as guests and gave them a draught that made them grow taller.
This character called a great assembly of his people that lasted three days.
This character led his people to break a dam and flood the stronghold of a wizard.

references.supports: Ents taught to speak by the Elves; the lost Entwives; Ent-draughts and Merry and Pippin's growth; the Entmoot; the flooding of Isengard.
The Ent-draughts taken by Merry and Pippin added three inches or more to their heights.

characters.name: Tom Bombadil
clues: This cheerful character wears a blue coat and yellow boots, and answers most questions in song.
This character's wife is the daughter of a river.
This character freed travelers from a malevolent willow and from a wight in a burial mound.
This character claims to have known the first raindrop and the first acorn.
This character put on the Ring without turning invisible, and it seemed to have no hold on him.

references.supports: Blue coat and yellow boots; Goldberry as River-daughter; rescue from Old Man Willow and the barrow-wight; the oldest, remembering the first raindrop and acorn; unaffected by the Ring.

characters.name: Gríma Wormtongue
clues: This character was a royal advisor whose silken words were more poison than counsel.
This character lusted after his king's niece and wanted to remove those who stood between them.
This character secretly served a wizard while holding a place of trust at a royal court.
From a high window, this character hurled a heavy dark globe at those standing below, nearly striking one of them.
In the end this character killed his former master on a doorstep in the Shire and was shot dead by hobbit archers.

references.supports: Royal advisor to Théoden; desire for Éowyn; agent of Saruman; threw the palantír from Orthanc; killed Saruman at Bag End and was shot by hobbits.

characters.name: Denethor
clues: This character was never a king, yet in all but name he ruled his realm for decades.
This character studied a seeing-stone in secret, until he saw only the hopeless things the Enemy chose to show.
This character loved his elder son and neglected the younger, who loved him dearly.
On receiving the shards of a broken horn, this character mourned his firstborn and began to sink into despair.
Driven mad by despair, this character tried to burn himself and his gravely wounded son on a pyre.

references.supports: Ruling Steward of Gondor; use of the Anor palantír and despair; preference for Boromir over Faramir; the broken Horn of Gondor; the pyre.

characters.name: Thorin Oakenshield
clues: Heir to a kingdom lost to a dragon, this character worked a humble trade in exile.
This character led a company of thirteen Dwarves, a wizard and a burglar on a long journey east.
A wizard gave this character a map and a key at the start of the quest.
Dragon-sickness took hold of this character inside the mountain, and he would not share the treasure.
Mortally wounded at the Battle of Five Armies, this character apologized to the burglar for his harsh words before he died.

references.supports: Exile in the Blue Mountains; led the company of thirteen; map and key from Gandalf; dragon-sickness; wounded at the Battle of Five Armies and apologized to Bilbo on his deathbed.

characters.name: Smaug
clues: Drawn by the wealth of a Dwarf kingdom, this creature drove its people into exile.
Asleep upon a hoard of treasure, this creature noticed that a single cup was missing and flew into a rage.
This creature's underside was crusted with gems, except for one bare patch that a thrush reported to an archer.
This creature burned a town built on a lake before it was slain.
A single black arrow, shot by an archer of Lake-town, killed this creature in the end.

references.supports: Attack on Erebor; theft of a cup; the bare patch on the underbelly and the thrush; destruction of Lake-town; slain by Bard with the Black Arrow.

characters.name: Beorn
clues: This character keeps bees and fine cattle in a wooden hall, and speaks to animals.
This character is a man by day, but a great black bear by night.
After suspicious questioning, this character sheltered a company of Dwarves for several days and lent them ponies.
This character arrived at a great battle just in time, in the shape of an enormous bear.
After the battle this character became a great chief and founded a line whose members were said to take bear-shape in times of need.

references.supports: Keeper of bees and cattle; changes between man and bear; hosted the Dwarves and lent ponies; fought at the Battle of Five Armies; became a great chief with bear-shifting descendants.

characters.name: Peregrin Took
clues: The youngest of a band of cousins, this character often spoke before thinking.
This character looked into a seeing-stone and was forced to face the Dark Lord's gaze.
This character pledged allegiance to the grieving Steward of Gondor and became a guard of his citadel.
At the Black Gate this character slew a troll, and was found crushed beneath its body.
Late in life this character became Thain of the Shire, and was later laid to rest in Gondor beside an old friend.

references.supports: Youngest of the four hobbits; looked in the Orthanc-stone; pledged allegiance to Denethor and became a Guard of the Citadel; killed a troll at the Black Gate; became Thain; buried in Rath Dínen.

characters.name: Fëanor
clues: This character's mother grew weary of life after his birth, and chose not to return to it.
This character crafted three jewels that held the light of the Two Trees.
With his seven sons, this character swore an oath that bound his house for ages.
This character burned the ships at Losgar, leaving part of his people behind on the far shore.
This character was mortally wounded by balrogs during the Battle-under-Stars, and his body burned to ash.

references.supports: Míriel's fading after his birth; the Silmarils; the Oath with his seven sons; burning of the ships at Losgar; death by Gothmog and balrogs in Dagor-nuin-Giliath.

characters.name: Fingolfin
clues: Half-brother of a rebellious smith, this character led the larger part of a host across a sea of ice.
After being left behind, this character crossed the frozen straits at the top of the world.
This character rode alone to a dark fortress and challenged its master to single combat.
This character wounded his foe seven times, and some of those wounds never fully healed.
This character fell to the Dark Lord after the duel, and the king of the Eagles carried his body to a mountaintop.

references.supports: Half-brother of Fëanor; crossing of the Helcaraxë; challenged Morgoth to single combat at Angband; wounded him seven times, his wounds never fully healing; body rescued by Thorondor and brought to a mountaintop.

characters.name: Túrin Turambar
clues: Sent away as a child by his mother, this character was fostered in an Elven kingdom.
A curse on this character's family was spoken by the Dark Lord himself, because of his father's defiance.
This character wielded a black sword that spoke at the last.
This character slew a dragon by crawling beneath it, but its dying words revealed a dreadful truth about his wife.
This character ended his own life by falling upon his sword after losing his family.

references.supports: Fostered in Doriath; Morgoth's curse on Húrin's kin; Gurthang; slaying of Glaurung and revelation about Níniel; death on his sword at Cabed-en-Aras.

characters.name: Eärendil
clues: Born in a hidden city, this character saw it fall as a child.
A ship built at the Havens by Elven shipwrights carried this character in search of the West.
This character's wife was the granddaughter of a famed mortal and an elven princess.
This character sailed into the uncharted West and pleaded there on behalf of Elves and Men.
Set in the heavens with a holy jewel on his brow, this character became a star seen at dusk and at dawn.

references.supports: Born in Gondolin and left to escape its fall; Vingilot built with Círdan; married Elwing, granddaughter of Beren and Lúthien; embassy to Valinor; set in the sky bearing a Silmaril.

characters.name: Beren
clues: A mortal outlaw, this character saw his father and his companions fall to a dark lord's hunters.
A ring given to this character's father by an elven king, in thanks for saving his life, became a family heirloom.
This character won the heart of an immortal maiden, and her father demanded a seemingly impossible price.
The price was a jewel from the Dark Lord's crown, and this character lost his hand to a great wolf.
After falling to the wolf, this character was allowed to return to life, and lived out his years with his wife.

references.supports: Barahir's band slain; Finrod's ring; Thingol's bride-price; the Silmaril and Carcharoth taking his hand; return from Mandos.

characters.name: Lúthien
clues: A king's daughter, this character was also the child of a being of divine race.
Her beauty was said to be the fairest that ever was among the children of the world.
With her song, this character cast a Dark Lord into a deep sleep.
This character was imprisoned by her own father in a house built among the branches of a great beech, and escaped by her magic.
This character chose to die like Men in order to share the fate of her husband.

references.supports: Daughter of Thingol and Melian; her beauty; put Morgoth to sleep with her song; the cloak of hair and escape from Hírilorn; chose mortality with Beren.
Thingol imprisoned Lúthien in a house among the branches of Hírilorn; she escaped using her magical arts.

characters.name: Finrod Felagund
clues: This character was the first of his people to meet Men, and he valued their friendship.
This character founded a vast underground fortress and ruled it for many years.
This character gave a ring as a pledge of friendship to a mortal who had saved his life.
This character matched songs against a dark lord's servant in a duel of power at a tower.
This character died in a dungeon at the hands of a werewolf, slain while saving a mortal companion.

references.supports: First Elf to meet Men; founded Nargothrond; ring given to Barahir; singing contest against Sauron; death in Tol-in-Gaurhoth fighting a werewolf to save Beren.

characters.name: Thingol
clues: This character stood spellbound in a woodland for years, and awoke as ruler of an Elven people.
This character's realm was protected by a girdle that nobody could cross without his leave.
This character set an impossible bride-price: a jewel from the crown of the Dark Lord.
Greed for a jewel set in a necklace led a party of Dwarves to murder this character.
After this character's death his wife left, the girdle fell, and his kingdom was ruined.

references.supports: Enchanted by Melian in Nan Elmoth; the Girdle of Melian; demanded a Silmaril of Beren; slain by Dwarves over the Nauglamír; Melian's departure and the ruin of Doriath.

characters.name: Círdan
clues: This character was among the oldest Elves still dwelling in Middle-earth at the end of the Third Age.
A master of ships, this character ruled a haven on the western coast.
This character gave a ring of fire to a newly arrived wizard.
This character helped build the ship in which a famous mariner sailed in search of the West.
This character prepared the last ship that bore the Ring-bearers over the Sea.

references.supports: Teleri Elf who stayed in Middle-earth; lord of the Grey Havens; gave Narya to Gandalf; helped with Eärendil's ship; the last ship carrying Frodo, Bilbo and Gandalf.

characters.name: Celebrimbor
clues: Grandson of the greatest of the Elven craftsmen, this character did not follow his father in his oath.
This character led the guild of Elven-smiths in a western realm called Hollin.
This character alone forged three rings that were kept free of the enemy's touch.
This character hid the three rings before his realm fell, and was tortured for their whereabouts.
After his death this character's body was displayed as a banner by the host that destroyed his realm.

references.supports: Grandson of Fëanor, stayed in Nargothrond against his father's oath; leader of the Gwaith-i-Mírdain; forged the Three; hid them; tortured and killed by Sauron; body used as a banner.

characters.name: Ungoliant
clues: The origins of this creature are a mystery, though some of the Elves suspected a spirit corrupted by the Dark Lord at the beginning of time.
This creature devoured light and spun darkness in its place.
This creature drained the Two Trees of their light and poisoned them.
This creature demanded the jewels the Dark Lord had stolen, and he refused her.
This creature's end is uncertain, but it is said she devoured herself in her hunger.

references.supports: Origins shrouded in mystery, thought by some Eldar to be an Ainu corrupted by Melkor; devoured light and spun Unlight; destroyed the Two Trees; Melkor refused her the jewels; said by some to have devoured herself.

characters.name: Elendil
clues: This character escaped the drowning of a great island with a fleet of ships.
This character led those of his people who had stayed faithful to the Valar.
This character founded two kingdoms in exile and was High King over both, ruling from the north.
This character fell in battle against the Dark Lord at the end of the Second Age, and his sword was broken beneath him.
This character's broken sword gave a shard that his son used to cut the Ring from the enemy's hand.

references.supports: Escaped the Downfall of Númenor; leader of the Faithful; High King of Arnor and Gondor (with Isildur and Anárion); death at the hand of Sauron and the shattering of Narsil; Isildur's use of the shard.
